rationale: C21 supplies a concrete and material drafting template. The child closely follows its distinctive section 22 sequence: the Secretary of Agriculture advises that imports threaten an agricultural program; the President causes the Tariff Commission to investigate; the Commission reports findings and recommendations; the President finds imports practically certain to interfere with the program; the President declares quantitative restrictions necessary; and the proclamation imposes limits on articles entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption. C16 is also highly similar, especially in its quantitative-quota and representative-period machinery, but C21 more closely matches the child's full recital sequence and statutory citation, including the 1951 amendment. C05 uses substantially similar section 22 findings but substitutes import fees for the child's quantitative quota.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Secretary of Agriculture has advised me that he has reason to believe that oats are being or are practically certain to be imported... as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the price-support program
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Secretary of Agriculture advised me that he had reason to believe that... the products... are practically certain to be imported... as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, programs undertaken by the Department of Agriculture
shared_material.explanation: Distinctively parallel initiating recital, with the same official, predictive import finding, and interference standard.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I caused the United States Tariff Commission to make an investigation under the said section 22... [and] the said Tariff Commission has made such investigation and has reported to me its findings and recommendations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I caused the United States Tariff Commission to make an investigation under the said section 22... [and] the said Tariff Commission has made such an investigation and has reported to me its findings and recommendations
shared_material.explanation: Nearly verbatim administrative sequence linking presidential referral, Commission investigation, and report.

shared_material.child_excerpt: on the basis of the said investigation and report of the Tariff Commission, I find that... [oats] are practically certain to be imported... under such conditions and in such quantities as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the said price-support program
shared_material.parent_excerpt: on the basis of the said investigation and report of the Tariff Commission, I find that... the articles... are practically certain to be imported... under such conditions and in such quantities as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, programs or operations undertaken by the Department of Agriculture
shared_material.explanation: Same operative factual finding, adapted from multiple agricultural articles and programs to oats and its price-support program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I find and declare that the imposition of quantitative limitations... is shown by such investigation of the Tariff Commission to be necessary in order that the entry, or withdrawal from warehouse, for consumption... will not render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the said price-support program
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I find and declare that... the imposition of the fees and quantitative limitations hereinafter proclaimed is shown by such investigation of the Tariff Commission to be necessary in order that the entry, or withdrawal from warehouse, for consumption... will not render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the said programs or operations
shared_material.explanation: Close literal reuse of the necessity finding and customs-entry machinery, narrowed to quantitative limits for oats.
